Question: Which of the following molecules has the shortest retention time in RP-HPLC at pH = 7?

Options:
A. Acetic acid
B. Toluene
C. Triethylamine

Thought: In RP-HPLC, molecules are separated based on their hydrophobicity. The stationary phase is non-polar (hydrophobic), while the mobile phase is more polar. Molecules that are more hydrophilic (polar) will have less interaction with the stationary phase and will elute faster, resulting in shorter retention times. Conversely, hydrophobic (non-polar) molecules will interact more strongly with the stationary phase and have longer retention times.

Let me analyze each molecule:

A. Acetic acid (CH3COOH): At pH 7, acetic acid (pKa ≈ 4.76) will be mostly in its deprotonated form (acetate, CH3COO-). The negatively charged acetate is hydrophilic and will have minimal interaction with the non-polar stationary phase.

B. Toluene (C7H8): This is a non-polar aromatic hydrocarbon with no charged or highly polar groups. It's hydrophobic and will interact strongly with the stationary phase.

C. Triethylamine ((CH3CH2)3N): At pH 7, triethylamine (pKa of conjugate acid ≈ 10.7) will be mostly in its neutral form, but it still has some polarity due to the nitrogen atom. It's less polar than acetic acid at pH 7 but more polar than toluene.

Based on hydrophobicity (from most to least hydrophobic):
Toluene > Triethylamine > Acetic acid (at pH 7)

Therefore, acetic acid would have the shortest retention time in RP-HPLC at pH 7.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
